The module tests (`03_Module_Contrasts`) say whether a module's summary moves. This step asks what
sits underneath and around it, five ways:

- hubs: each module's most central proteins and how each changed;
- coupling: whether two modules change together across people, within HR and within LR;
- rewiring: whether a protein belongs to its module in one group and not the other;
- per person: each person's module changes, ordered by how much they grew;
- PLS: whether the modules together separate HR from LR or predict growth.

Every result here is exploratory: 8 people per group, and nothing below is corrected across the
whole step. The figures are in `04_Figures/Modules`.

## Packages

```{r}
#| label: packages
#| message: false
library(here)
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(purrr)
library(WGCNA)
source(here("02_HRvLR", "helpers.R"))
source(here("00_Setup", "Shared_functions", "workbooks.R"))
disableWGCNAThreads()
inputs <- c(
  modules = "01_Processing/06_Module_Building/c_data/modules.rds",
  corrected = "01_Processing/03_Blood_Correction/c_data/proteins_corrected.rds",
  contrasts = "02_HRvLR/01_Protein_Contrasts/c_data/protein_contrasts.xlsx",
  phenotype = "00_Setup/Input/phenotype.csv"
)
paths <- vapply(inputs, here, character(1))
stopifnot(file.exists(paths))
```

## Input

```{r}
#| label: input
modules <- readRDS(paths[["modules"]])
corrected <- readRDS(paths[["corrected"]])
results <- readxl::read_excel(paths[["contrasts"]], "protein_by_contrast")
phenotype <- readr::read_csv(paths[["phenotype"]], show_col_types = FALSE)
meta <- modules$meta
me <- modules$eigengenes
members <- filter(modules$membership, module != "grey")
group_of <- with(phenotype, set_names(group, subject))
stopifnot(
  identical(colnames(me), meta$sample_id), identical(colnames(corrected$E), meta$sample_id),
  setequal(names(group_of), meta$subject)
)
dim(me)
```

## Hubs

A protein's kME is its correlation with its module's eigengene; the highest are the module's hubs.
Each module's 15 hubs are joined to their logFC, p and FDR in the six training and acute contrasts
(each group and the interaction).

```{r}
#| label: hubs
hub_contrasts <- c(
  "Training_HR", "Training_LR", "Training_Interaction", "Acute_HR", "Acute_LR", "Acute_Interaction"
)
hubs <- members |>
  slice_max(kme, n = 15, by = module, with_ties = FALSE) |>
  mutate(hub_rank = row_number(), .by = module) |>
  inner_join(
    filter(results, contrast %in% hub_contrasts) |> select(uniprot_id, contrast, logFC, p, fdr),
    by = "uniprot_id"
  ) |>
  arrange(module, hub_rank, match(contrast, hub_contrasts))
count(filter(hubs, p < 0.05), contrast)
```

## Coupling

For each window (training: T2 − T1; acute: T3 − T2) and group, the Spearman correlation between
two modules' eigengene changes across the 8 people. The HR − LR difference per pair is tested with
Fisher's z on the two correlations (each from 8 people), which treats Spearman's rho as Pearson's;
with 8 people this is a rough guide.

```{r}
#| label: coupling
changes <- list(
  training = person_values(me, meta, "T2", from = "T1"),
  acute = person_values(me, meta, "T3", from = "T2")
)
fisher_p <- \(r1, r2, n) 2 * pnorm(-abs((atanh(r1) - atanh(r2)) / sqrt(2 / (n - 3))))
pairs <- combn(rownames(me), 2) |>
  t() |>
  as_tibble(.name_repair = ~ c("module_a", "module_b"))
coupling <- imap(changes, \(x, window) {
  rho <- map(c(HR = "HR", LR = "LR"), \(g) {
    cor(t(x[, names(group_of)[group_of == g]]), method = "spearman")
  })
  mutate(pairs,
    window,
    rho_HR = rho$HR[cbind(module_a, module_b)], rho_LR = rho$LR[cbind(module_a, module_b)],
    difference = rho_HR - rho_LR,
    p_difference = fisher_p(pmin(rho_HR, 0.999), pmin(rho_LR, 0.999), 8)
  )
}) |>
  list_rbind() |>
  relocate(window)
filter(coupling, p_difference < 0.05)
```

## Rewiring

Each member's kME is recomputed within HR's 24 biopsies and within LR's 24, on the person-centred
values that built the modules (`06_Module_Building`). A protein with a high kME in one group and a
low one in the other moves with its module in one group only.

```{r}
#| label: rewiring
centred <- apply(corrected$E, 1, \(v) v - ave(v, meta$subject))
colours <- with(modules$membership, set_names(module, uniprot_id))[colnames(centred)]
group_kme <- map(c(HR = "HR", LR = "LR"), \(g) {
  rows <- meta$group == g
  eigen <- moduleEigengenes(centred[rows, ], colors = colours, excludeGrey = TRUE)$eigengenes
  k <- signedKME(centred[rows, ], eigen,
    corFnc = "bicor", corOptions = "maxPOutliers = 0.05, pearsonFallback = 'individual'"
  )
  colnames(k) <- sub("^kME", "", colnames(k))
  k
})
rewiring <- members |>
  transmute(
    module, uniprot_id, gene, kme,
    kme_HR = group_kme$HR[cbind(uniprot_id, module)],
    kme_LR = group_kme$LR[cbind(uniprot_id, module)], shift = kme_HR - kme_LR
  ) |>
  arrange(module, desc(abs(shift)))
slice_max(rewiring, abs(shift), n = 2, by = module)
```

## Per person

Each person's eigengene change per module and window, with their group and growth score (the
composite that ranked them into HR and LR).

```{r}
#| label: per-person
per_person <- imap(changes, \(x, window) {
  as_tibble(t(x), rownames = "subject") |> mutate(window = window)
}) |>
  list_rbind() |>
  pivot_longer(-c(subject, window), names_to = "module", values_to = "change") |>
  left_join(select(phenotype, subject, group, comp_hypertrophy), by = "subject") |>
  relocate(window, subject, group, comp_hypertrophy)
summarise(per_person, spread = round(sd(change), 3), .by = c(window, module)) |> head()
```

## PLS

Sparse PLS (mixOmics) on the eigengenes: sPLS-DA for HR against LR from the T1 levels, the
training change and the acute change; sPLS regression for the % gains in fibre area, muscle area
and leg press, and the growth score, from the T1 levels and the training change. One component;
the number of modules kept (2, 4, 6 or all) is tuned by 3-fold cross-validation inside each
training set, and the outer loop is 4-fold cross-validation repeated 5 times. Folds for sPLS-DA hold
out HR and LR people in equal numbers: with leave-one-out, a model with no signal predicts against
the held-out person's group (removing one person tilts the training set to the other), which pushes
AUCs below 0.5. The score is the AUC (sPLS-DA) or Q² = 1 − held-out error / error of the training
mean (sPLS-R), averaged over repeats. The null reruns the whole procedure (2 repeats) on 1,000
shuffles of the outcome; p = (1 + null ≥ observed) / 1,001. The loadings come from one model on all
16 people.

```{r}
#| label: pls
people <- colnames(changes$training)
windows <- list(
  T1 = t(person_values(me, meta, "T1"))[people, ], training = t(changes$training),
  acute = t(changes$acute)
)
gains <- trait_windows(phenotype)$training
keep_grid <- c(2, 4, 6, nrow(me))
auc <- \(score, y) {
  r <- rank(score)
  hr <- y == "HR"
  (sum(r[hr]) - sum(hr) * (sum(hr) + 1) / 2) / (sum(hr) * sum(!hr))
}
fit_da <- \(x, y, k) mixOmics::splsda(x, y, ncomp = 1, keepX = k)
fit_reg <- \(x, y, k) mixOmics::spls(x, y, ncomp = 1, keepX = k, mode = "regression")
predict_da <- \(fit, x) predict(fit, x)$predict[, "HR", 1]
predict_reg <- \(fit, x) predict(fit, x)$predict[, 1, 1]
# Fold labels: balanced across HR and LR for a factor, random for a number.
folds_of <- function(y, k) {
  if (!is.factor(y)) {
    return(sample(rep_len(seq_len(k), length(y))))
  }
  folds <- integer(length(y))
  for (g in levels(y)) folds[y == g] <- sample(rep_len(seq_len(k), sum(y == g)))
  folds
}
# Held-out predictions from one pass of 4-fold CV, the panel size tuned by 3-fold CV inside each
# training set; `base` is each held-out person's training mean, for Q2.
cv_pass <- function(x, y, fit, predict_one, loss) {
  outer <- folds_of(y, 4)
  pred <- base <- numeric(length(y))
  for (f in 1:4) {
    train <- outer != f
    xt <- x[train, , drop = FALSE]
    yt <- y[train]
    inner <- folds_of(yt, 3)
    tuned <- map_dbl(keep_grid, \(k) {
      held <- numeric(length(yt))
      for (g in 1:3) {
        held[inner == g] <- predict_one(
          fit(xt[inner != g, , drop = FALSE], yt[inner != g], k), xt[inner == g, , drop = FALSE]
        )
      }
      loss(held, yt)
    })
    pred[!train] <- predict_one(fit(xt, yt, keep_grid[which.min(tuned)]), x[!train, , drop = FALSE])
    if (!is.factor(y)) base[!train] <- mean(yt)
  }
  list(pred = pred, base = base)
}
score <- function(model, x, y, repeats) {
  mean(map_dbl(seq_len(repeats), \(r) {
    if (model == "sPLS-DA") {
      auc(cv_pass(x, y, fit_da, predict_da, \(s, yt) 1 - auc(s, yt))$pred, y)
    } else {
      cv <- cv_pass(x, y, fit_reg, predict_reg, \(p, yt) sum((yt - p)^2))
      1 - sum((y - cv$pred)^2) / sum((y - cv$base)^2)
    }
  }))
}
outcome_of <- \(outcome) {
  if (outcome == "HR vs LR") factor(group_of[people], c("LR", "HR"))
  else gains[[outcome]][match(people, gains$subject)]
}
tasks <- bind_rows(
  tibble(model = "sPLS-DA", window = names(windows), outcome = "HR vs LR"),
  expand_grid(
    model = "sPLS-R", window = c("T1", "training"),
    outcome = c("pct_fcsa_mixed", "pct_mcsa", "pct_leg_press_1rm", "comp_hypertrophy")
  )
)
RNGkind("L'Ecuyer-CMRG")
set.seed(20261028)
n_perm <- 1000
pls_fits <- pmap(tasks, \(model, window, outcome) {
  x <- windows[[window]]
  y <- outcome_of(outcome)
  observed <- score(model, x, y, 5)
  null <- unlist(parallel::mclapply(seq_len(n_perm), \(b) score(model, x, sample(y), 2),
    mc.cores = max(1, parallel::detectCores() - 1), mc.set.seed = TRUE
  ))
  full <- if (model == "sPLS-DA") {
    mixOmics::splsda(x, y, ncomp = 1)
  } else {
    mixOmics::spls(x, y, ncomp = 1, mode = "regression")
  }
  list(
    summary = tibble(
      model, window, outcome, statistic = if (model == "sPLS-DA") "AUC" else "Q2", observed,
      null_median = median(null), null_95 = unname(quantile(null, 0.95)),
      p_perm = (1 + sum(null >= observed)) / (1 + n_perm)
    ),
    loadings = tibble(model, window, outcome,
      module = rownames(full$loadings$X), loading = full$loadings$X[, 1]
    )
  )
})
pls <- list_rbind(map(pls_fits, "summary"))
pls_loadings <- list_rbind(map(pls_fits, "loadings"))
pls
```

## Validation

```{r}
#| label: validate
stopifnot(
  all(count(hubs, module)$n == 15 * length(hub_contrasts)),
  nrow(coupling) == 2 * nrow(pairs), all(abs(c(coupling$rho_HR, coupling$rho_LR)) <= 1),
  nrow(rewiring) == nrow(members), !anyNA(rewiring$kme_HR), !anyNA(rewiring$kme_LR),
  nrow(per_person) == 2 * length(people) * nrow(me),
  nrow(pls) == nrow(tasks), all(pls$p_perm > 0 & pls$p_perm <= 1)
)
```

## Summary

`r sum(coupling$p_difference < 0.05)` of `r nrow(coupling)` module pairs couple differently in
HR and LR at Fisher p < 0.05. The largest kME shift is `r rewiring$gene[which.max(abs(rewiring$shift))]`
in `r rewiring$module[which.max(abs(rewiring$shift))]` (HR
`r round(rewiring$kme_HR[which.max(abs(rewiring$shift))], 2)`, LR
`r round(rewiring$kme_LR[which.max(abs(rewiring$shift))], 2)`). The best PLS model is
`r with(slice_min(pls, p_perm, n = 1, with_ties = FALSE), sprintf("%s, %s, %s: %s %.2f, permutation p %.3f", model, window, outcome, statistic, observed, p_perm))`.

## Save

```{r}
#| label: save
out <- here("02_HRvLR", "08_Module_Detail", "c_data")
dir.create(out, showWarnings = FALSE)
detail <- list(
  hubs = hubs, coupling = coupling, rewiring = rewiring, per_person = per_person, pls = pls,
  pls_loadings = pls_loadings
)
saveRDS(detail, file.path(out, "module_detail.rds"))
write_workbook(
  detail,
  c(
    "Per module, its 15 highest-kME proteins with logFC, p and FDR in six contrasts.",
    "Per window and module pair: Spearman rho of eigengene changes in HR and in LR, Fisher p.",
    "Per member: kME overall, within HR and within LR biopsies, and HR minus LR.",
    "Per window, person and module: eigengene change, group and growth score.",
    "Per PLS task: held-out AUC or Q2, its permutation null and p.",
    "Per PLS task and module: component-1 loading on all 16 people."
  ),
  file.path(out, "module_detail.xlsx"), inputs, paths
)
```
